params.body:
A post published in Sanity started a Netlify build, the build finished, and the site still showed the previous text. It happened three times on 19 November 2026, with a title, an opening paragraph and a gallery photo. A second build a minute later showed the new content each time.

## Cause

`query()` in `src/lib/sanity.js` read from `apicdn.sanity.io`, Sanity's cached API. The Sanity webhook starts the build at the moment of publishing, and for a short while after a publish the cache can still answer with the previous version. Checked directly during one of the three: `api.sanity.io` returned the new text while the built site had the old one.

## Change

`query()` now reads from `api.sanity.io`, the live API. It is only called at build time, a handful of requests per build, so the cache bought nothing there.

Not changed: the browser-side fetches in the pages (campaign and price widgets) and `src/lib/pricing.js` still use the cached API.

## Checked

- `npm test`: 25 passed. `npm run build` and `npm run check:built`: no contact number.
- The build output lists the news post and the homepage's latest-news block as before.
params.title: Build reads Sanity's live API, so a build started by a publish sees that publish
